title: Kernel ↔ Batching Bridge — standup notes Mar 9-12 2026
content: Purpose: capture daily syncs across kernel, batching, and infra teams while we prototype the kernel↔batching bridge that surfaces per-request cache heuristics to the batching layer.
Attendees: Ava (owner), Liam, Sofia, Noah, Maya, Ezra, plus SRE: Priya Rao (ad-hoc).

Summary: Three-day focused iteration to get an end-to-end light-weight prototype: 1) add a small control plane in kernel to label requests with 'kv_hint' metadata, 2) extend batch router to prioritize KV-friendly merges, 3) run small perf harness against 2.7B and 13B quantized model variants.

High-level outcome so far: bridge prototype is functional end-to-end. Observed p95 generation latency improvement of ~8–12% for KV-hot request flows under synthetic trace; mixed results on KV-warm/warm->cold transitions. See experiment logs below.

Risks/concerns flagged: 1) metadata adds 24–40 bytes per request; impact on throughput when batching at 8K tokens needs careful accounting. 2) Race window when kernel signals a cache miss then batching coalesces requests — could increase cold-start amplification.
Decisions made during sync:
- Keep bridge metadata schema minimal: kv_hint = {hot|warm|cold} (string), kv_version (small integer). Avoid adding full key fingerprints at this stage.
- Use optimistic batching: batch router will tentatively merge differing kv_hint values but will prefer to group 'hot' with 'hot' at colocated queues once measured throughput drop >5%.
- Rollout plan: keep prototype behind the 'bridge-experiment' feature flag; do not enable on production tenants until perf is stable in staging for 48h.
Daily notes — 2026-03-09:
- Ava: wired kernel metadata outflow (PR#842). Simple header injection at request envelope boundary. Local unit tests pass.
- Liam: batch router change implemented to read kv_hint and attempt candidate grouping. Need to add metrics for 'merged_hint_mismatch' and 'merge_rejection_reason'.
- Sofia: wrote first perf harness that replays a 10k-request trace derived from production sampled traces (anonymized). Initial run shows p50 unchanged, p95 down by 9% for hot-heavy slices.
Daily notes — 2026-03-10:
- Noah: debugged a corner case where kv_version mismatch caused kv cache lookups to be skipped. Added a simple backoff to avoid immediate rekey churn.
- Maya: profiled CPU cost of metadata serialization. Observed +0.6% CPU at batch size 8; +1.9% at size 32. Added micro-optimizations to avoid JSON allocations (use compact binary header).
- Action: swap header format to length-prefixed binary tag in kernel branch to reduce allocation pressure. Assigned to Maya, target by 2026-03-12.
Daily notes — 2026-03-11:

- Ezra: ran long-run stability test (6h) in staging with mixed traffic. Found two incidents of request re-ordering leading to slight token duplication for a single request path. Root cause: router's optimistic merge and per-queue token accounting. Mitigation: add an in-flight request id check to prevent duplicate emission.
- SRE (Priya): advised to add an emergency kill-switch metric 'bridge_merge_rate' and an alert if merge_rate spikes by >200% or error_rate > 0.2% for 5m.
Experiment log (summary of runs):
- Run A (hot-heavy): model 2.7B q4_0, batch sizes adaptive capped at 16. p95 baseline: 112ms; with bridge: 101ms (-11%). throughput +6%. notes: good where kv_hot proportion > 60%.

- Run B (mixed): model 13B q4_1, synthetic mix 40% hot / 40% warm / 20% cold. p95 baseline: 210ms; with bridge: 198ms (-6%). throughput neutral. notes: marginal win but cold transitions created 1.2x token tail in 3% of requests.

- Run C (cold-heavy): model 13B, cold proportion 75%. p95 showed slight regression +4% with bridge (due to increased merge attempts causing cold-start contention). Decision: add adaptive merge throttling when cold_fraction > 60%.
Open items / TODOs (owners):
- (Maya) Finish binary header switch and bench serialization cost — due 2026-03-12.
- (Liam) Add 'merged_hint_mismatch' metric and a Grafana panel — due 2026-03-14.
- (Noah) Implement in-flight request id dedupe in router, run short smoke tests — due 2026-03-12.
- (Sofia) Expand replay trace to include multi-turn chat patterns and longer KV reuse windows; run overnight — due 2026-03-13.
- (Ava) Draft short one-pager for eng leadership summarizing prototype results and proposed ramp plan to dedicated tenants — due 2026-03-15.
Blocked items:
- We need a small infra change to increase staging queue depth to reproduce high-batch scenarios. Blocked on infra ticket INF-2246; SRE acknowledged priority but ETA is 3 days.
Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a hybrid eviction hint: kernel could emit 'kv_prefetchable' when it predicts next tokens will likely hit KV again; router could then bias groups to increase cache locality.
- If binary header addition is cheap enough, consider adding a compact probabilistic fingerprint for stronger grouping without leaking keys.
- Ops: test the feature flag flow (enable -> sample 1% -> 10% -> 100% in staging) and ensure metrics are available at each bump.
Decisions / Next steps (short list):
- Complete serialization and dedupe mitigations in next 72h.
- Add merge throttling heuristic for cold-heavy mixes and re-run cold-heavy scenario.
- Prepare a staging-only canary (1% traffic) for next week once infra queue depth change lands.
Appendix: quick references

- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (kernel header prototype), issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/issues/1176 (router merge telemetry), JIRA: JIRA-RT-1192 (bridge experiment epic).
- Slack thread: #serve-runtime-kv-batching — tag 'bridge-experiment' for visibility.
End of notes. Last updated 2026-03-12 by Ava Martinez.
